newsitem.title: INDIA: India's SEBI panel suggests changes in issue norms.
newsitem.headline: India's SEBI panel suggests changes in issue norms.

text.p: Companies should be allowed to issue equity at par value, an advisory committee set up by the market regulator Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) said on Thursday.
"It would enable the companies to issue shares at their intrinsic value instead of at a minimum price of 10 rupees," SEBI said in a statement.
The lock-in period for promoters' contributions needs to be reduced to three years from five, the committee said.

The committee agreed to continue with a minimum 90 percent subscription requirment for new issues but suggested promoters be given the opportunity to make up for shortfalls on equity offers that were not underwritten.
Shares issued to employees on preferential basis must be subject to a lock-in period, it said.
SEBI said it would examine the panel's suggestions before taking a decision whether to adopt them.
